decisions.reason: Assigning mint #1 to a specific Base-compatible address does not change the required blockchain network.
The requested transfer of mint #1 does not change which NFT state must transfer during a secondary sale.
Ownership of mint #1 has no effect on the secondary-sale royalty amount, enforcement, allocation, or marketplace policy.
Designating the recipient of mint #1 does not change the NFT asset type, unlimited supply, price, or mint-number identifier.
The request is consistent with numbering beginning at 1 but does not change the migration, legacy-state, or redeployment policy.
Transferring mint #1 to the founder does not alter the required metadata fields or their accuracy rules.
The destination of an already designated mint does not change the ETH payment, swap, output-target, or shortfall behavior.
The source requests an individual NFT transfer and does not require the FAQ to disclose or explain ownership of mint #1.
The existing rule already requires the dashboard to reflect actual ownership; naming a transfer destination does not modify that general rule.
The designated recipient would be covered by the existing NFT-holder access policy, which remains unchanged.
Ownership of affiliate code #1 changes the holder instance, not the existing rule that commissions go to the holder associated with the code used.
The transfer destination does not change how commissions or earnings must be counted or displayed.
